newsitem.title: USA: Florida pilot indicted for smuggling Cuban cigars.
newsitem.headline: Florida pilot indicted for smuggling Cuban cigars.

text.p: A Florida airline pilot has been indicted on charges of trying to smuggle 121 boxes of Cuban cigars into the United States in violation of the U.S. embargo on Cuba, the U.S. Attorney General's office said on Wednesday.
Christopher Plummer, 35, appeared in a Fort Lauderdale federal court on Tuesday and was released on $100,000 bail pending trial.
Plummer was arrested last August after customs agents and Coast Guard officers boarded his fishing boat 13 miles west of Bimini for a routine inspection, the indictment said.
They seized more than 3,000 Cuban cigars, including premium brands such as Cohiba and Montecristo, valued at $50,000.

Plummer, a pilot with Bahamas-based Paradise Air, lives in Fort Lauderdale. If convicted, he faces up to 15 years in jail and a fine of up to $300,000 for violating the Trading with the Enemy Act, the attorney general's office said.
Customs officials say smuggling of Cuban cigars into the United States has soared because of a current fashion for cigar smoking.
